rows.judge_notes: The biggest gap is that there is no real payment integration: charges and refunds are an inline mock card check plus a database field, with no provider abstraction and no signed, idempotent webhooks; in addition spec.md is just the one-sentence request with no journeys, the README is one line, there is no health endpoint, login has no brute-force limit, and sessions are lost on restart. The strongest part is the core booking loop: the server sets the price, a seat is only confirmed after the charge succeeds, the capacity check and insert run synchronously so concurrent requests cannot overbook, writes go through a temp file and rename, the UI is clean, accessible and safe against XSS, and all 21 HTTP and Playwright tests pass. Sellable: no, not until a real payment provider, a proper spec, ops docs and login rate limiting are added.

The biggest gap is that the Stripe adapter has only been tested against a fake fetch, never live Stripe, and the app sends no emails, has an in-memory per-email login throttle, and runs as one SQLite process, so the first live test-mode payment and refund are still unproven. The strongest part is the payment and booking core: the server sets the price, seats are held inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions, booking state changes only on signature-checked webhooks, late or duplicate payments are refunded with idempotency keys, and all 96 node --test tests pass and cover C1–C11 and O1–O6 over real HTTP, including 10 concurrent bookings for 3 seats. Sellable: yes, to a small studio as a single-instance deployment, after one end-to-end Stripe test-mode run.
